questions.prompt: The sponsor says: run costs for the first year are capped at SAR 1.2 million, the approved budget line. How do you record it?
options: As a driver, with a scenario that measures spend
As a constraint, with the sponsor as its owner
As a concern of the finance and cost lead
As an assumption to test with the pilot
questions.explanation: The cap is a decision already taken that bounds every option; nobody builds the system to spend it.
misconceptions: Treats a limit as a goal: the system does not exist to spend SAR 1.2 million
Mistakes a fixed decision for a worry: the cap is approved, not feared
Confuses an approved budget with a belief: nothing about it needs testing

questions.prompt: Three interviews are done. Which note most deserves a second reading before any design is drawn?
options: The sponsor's target for the permit cycle
The product owner's wish for a dark staff console
The data protection officer's remark that applicant files do not leave the Kingdom
The brief's sentence that the assistant must be fast and accurate
questions.explanation: A placement constraint said in passing rules out whole designs, so it is found before options are drawn.
misconceptions: Thinks drivers rule designs out: a target shapes the options but forbids none
Gives weight to noise: no architecture decision depends on the console colour
Confuses vague targets with constraints: they need numbers, not a second reading

questions.prompt: Which response measure turns the inspectors' concern (only an inspector approves) into a testable scenario?
options: The prompt says that only inspectors approve
Answers never sound like an approval
At least 99% of all answers include a contact number
At least 99% of approval questions receive an offer of a person
questions.explanation: It names the slice, the metric, the statistic and the target, so a reviewer can compute it from logs.
misconceptions: Mistakes a design choice for a measured response
States an intent with no metric or statistic
Measures the wrong population: approval questions are diluted among all answers

questions.prompt: In 400 pilot requests, one answer showed another applicant's deed. Which privacy measure should the scenario use?
options: The number of such answers, with a target of zero
The mean leak rate, with a target below 1%
The p95 of leaks per day
The share of answers that cite a clause
questions.explanation: A single leak is an incident; a sum with a target of zero fails on it, a mean of 0.25% hides it.
misconceptions: Lets a rate hide a harm that counts one by one
Uses a latency statistic for an event count
Measures transparency, not privacy

questions.prompt: A summary job combines published zoning maps with the names and mobile numbers of engineering office contacts. Under the highest-level principle, what is the job's output?
options: Public, because most of it is published
Restricted, because it holds personal data
Secret, because it combines two sources
Unclassified until the job runs
questions.explanation: A set that combines levels takes the highest; contact persons are personal data and Restricted in the case.
misconceptions: Takes the level of the largest part instead of the highest
Thinks combining raises the level by itself
Ignores that data is classified when it is created

questions.prompt: The p95s of the hops of a request add up to 4,290 ms; the end-to-end p95 measured in the pilot is 4,866 ms. What explains the gap?
options: The sum of p95s always overstates, so the measurement is wrong
Retries and queues add time that no single hop's percentile shows
The asynchronous log write was left out of the sum
p50s should have been added instead
questions.explanation: The sum of p95s bounds the hops; retries and queueing between hops add time the per-hop numbers miss.
misconceptions: Trusts the bound over the measurement
Adds a hop users never wait for
A sum of medians understates the tail even more

questions.prompt: Why does the course write the hosting of every container on the container view?
options: So the sponsor sees which vendor was chosen
Because Mermaid requires a hosting label
So a reviewer can check placement against the classified flows by reading the view
Because the context view cannot show external systems
questions.explanation: Hosting on the boxes lets placement be read and diffed with the view.
misconceptions: Mistakes a vendor choice for the placement question
Confuses a course convention with a tool rule
The context view does show external systems

questions.prompt: The inspections team wants its standard letters drafted in the house style from inspector notes; 9,000 approved letters exist. The building code changes monthly. What does fine-tuning give them, and what must still come from elsewhere?
options: Both the style and the current code requirements
The style; the facts come from the inspector's notes
Nothing a prompt cannot give
The current code requirements; the style comes from a template
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning shapes a stable form from many examples; facts that change come from the notes or retrieval.
misconceptions: Thinks tuning keeps knowledge current: the next circular makes a tuned model wrong
Ignores what 9,000 examples make possible; a prompt is a rival to test, not a certainty
Inverts the two: tuning is for form, retrieval for knowledge that changes

questions.prompt: Option O3 has the lowest build and run cost but answers 70% of questions, against 92% for O1. Why can its three-year cost still be the highest?
options: Its build cost is paid every year
Unanswered questions become calls the Ministry also pays for
Non-generative systems need more servers
Its token price is higher
questions.explanation: The cost model counts the calls created by unanswered questions; at 30% unanswered they dominate.
misconceptions: Build is a first-year line only
O3 runs on fixed infrastructure with no capacity units
O3 has no tokens at all

questions.prompt: Doubling the token price moves O1's three-year total by 3%; the high volume forecast moves it by 58%. What belongs in the decision's review trigger?
options: The token price only
A monthly request volume, then the price
The build cost
Nothing: O1 is cheapest
questions.explanation: The ranking depends most on volume, so the trigger watches volume first and price second.
misconceptions: Watches the input with the least effect
Build is spent and cannot reopen the decision
A cheapest option today can stop being cheapest; that is what triggers are for

questions.prompt: With exit cost weighted 0.10, O1 scores 4.20 and O2 4.10; at 0.13, O2 leads. What should the options paper do?
options: Report O1 as the winner and omit the flip
Raise the exit weight until the preferred option wins
Report the ranking and the flip weight, and record the fragility as a bad consequence
Drop weighted scoring from the paper
questions.explanation: Weights are opinions; a close ranking is reported with the weight that reverses it.
misconceptions: Presents an opinion as a fact
Tunes weights to a conclusion
Throws away a useful method instead of reporting its sensitivity

questions.prompt: Which procurement requirement can a reviewer verify?
options: The provider will support a smooth exit
The provider shall make reasonable efforts to export data
The provider shall export all indexed documents in JSON Lines within 10 working days of a request
The provider should prefer open formats
questions.explanation: It uses 'shall', names a format and a time a reviewer can test.
misconceptions: Uses 'will' and no measurable term
Contains an escape phrase
Uses 'should' and no testable term

options: If the situation changes materially
When the team has time to revisit
If monthly requests exceed 600,000 in the gateway logs
When quality seems lower than expected
questions.explanation: It names a measurement, a threshold and where it is measured.
misconceptions: No measurement
No measurement or date
A feeling, not a threshold
